courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Periodontal Therapy
courses.description: This graduate seminar reviews techniques and procedures for treating periodontal diseases. Topics include gingival grafting, surgical flap management, osseous surgery, periodontal regeneration, antimicrobials, host modulation, and periodontal medicine.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Case Analysis
courses.description: This graduate seminar continues themes introduced in PERI 720 and discusses advanced implant topics including bone augmentation, peri-implantitis, and implant efficacy assessment. The seminar includes didactic lectures, case presentations, and journal club components. Spring.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Seminar in Periodontology
courses.description: In this first-year literature review course, graduate students present and evaluate the evidence on periodontal disease etiology, pathogenesis, risk factors and treatments including mechanical, surgical, and pharmacological approaches.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Seminar in Periodontology
courses.description: In this second- and third-year literature review course, graduate students discuss evidence on advanced topics in periodontology or related disciplines.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Introduction to Implants
courses.description: This graduate seminar traces the biology of osseointegration, surgical techniques in dental implant placement, and prosthetic restoration. The seminar includes didactic lectures, case presentations, and journal club components.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Clinical Implantology
courses.description: This graduate seminar continues themes introduced in PERI 820 and discusses advanced implant topics including bone augmentation, peri-implantitis, and implant efficacy assessment. The seminar includes didactic lectures, case presentations, and journal club components.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Advanced Clinical Periodontics and Clinical Practice
courses.description: Within this specialty clinic, graduate students gain experience and competency in diagnosing and comprehensively treating patients with periodontal diseases. Cases may involve interdisciplinary care, medical management, dental implants, and sedation procedures.

courses.subject: PERI
courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: Individual research under the direction of a mentor with the intention of publication. Completion of a manuscript and publication is a requirement for an MS degree.
